entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Coram: Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Harkesh Manuja
Present: Mr. Gunjan Mehta, Addl. A.G. Punjab.

****
 Harkesh Manuja,
 Manuja J. (Oral)

By way of present appeal, appeal, challenge has been laid to the award dated 30.08.1993 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, Patiala, Patiala whereby the reference rence petition filed under Section 18 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act') by the landowners for seeking enhancement of market value of the acquired land was partly allowed.

2. Briefly stating, land measuring 3.69 acres situated within the revenue estate of Village Gadomajra, Tehsil Rajpura, District Patiala was acquired for the public purpose namely for construction of Mirzapur Distributory vide notifications dated 11.03.1990 and 11.03.1987 issued under Sections 4 and 6 respectively of the Act.
Subsequently, the he Land Acquisition Collector (for short short 'LAC') passed Award N No.239 dated 23.10.1987.

3. The landowners, feeling dissatisfied with the said award, sought reference under Section 18 of the Act and the learned Reference Court enhanced the amount of compensation to Rs.1,00,000/- per acre for chahi land and Rs.60,000/ Rs.60,000/- per acre for Gair Mumkin land..
4.
Aggrieved of the aforesaid award dated 30.08.1993,, the present Regular First Appeal (RFA) has been filed at the instance of appellant.

sentences.text: I have heard learned counsel for the parties and gone through the paper-book.
I am unable to find substance in the submission made on behalf of the appellant-State.
6. In the present case, acquisition was carried out for the public purpose for construction of Mirzapur Distributory.

From the deposition of AW-3 namely, Jagat Singh, Kanungo, O/o LAC, it has been established on record that as a result of acquisition, neither any source of irrigation was left for the landowners nor any passage was left going from one tak of land to the other tak of land except a bridge which was at a distance of  kilometer from their holdings.

Moreover, the benefit of damage towards severance @ 60% of market value of unacquired land across canal and 40% of market value of unacquired land towards village side has been based on an earlier decision made by this Court in case of "Tehal Singh Vs. State of Punjab", reported as "1987 LACC, 491".

entities.text: Tehal Singh Vs. State of Punjab", reported as "1987 LACC, 491
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 7. In view of the aforesaid, the judgment dated 30.08.1993 passed by the learned Reference Court calls for no interference and the present appeal being devoid of merits is thus, dismissed.
04.12.2025 (HARKESH MANUJA)
